coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert
setup:
Position a key forward and key defender in a marking contest.
Place two small forwards outside the landing area.
Position one additional defender at ground level.
The coach delivers the football to the aerial contest.
The mark is spoiled or allowed to spill.
The key forward must recover and assess whether to collect, protect or direct the football.
Small forwards move through receive gates.
Rotate aerial and ground-level roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach delivers the football to the marking contest.
The key forward competes in the air.
The football spills to ground.
The forward lands and locates the football.
The player competes with the key defender for recovery position.
If clean possession is available, the forward gathers and protects.
A small forward communicates and moves past the contest.
The key forward handballs or directs the football to the small forward.
The receiver finishes at goal.
If defenders win possession, forwards apply immediate pressure.
coachingPoints: Recover immediately after the aerial contest.
Use body size and strength legally to protect the drop zone.
Take clean possession when possible.
Do not attempt to turn through multiple defenders unnecessarily.
Small forwards must remain outside the key forward’s feet.
Release into the runner’s path.
Continue protecting or shepherding after disposal.
Apply forward pressure after turnover.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the key forward lands safely.
Whether the spill is located immediately.
Whether body position protects the football.
Whether possession is taken when available.
Whether small forwards remain outside congestion.
Whether the release leads the receiver.
Whether the key forward continues supporting.
Whether defensive pressure follows turnover.

commonErrors.error: The key forward remains focused on the missed mark.
commonErrors.correction: Recover immediately and locate the ground ball.

commonErrors.error: The player attempts to turn through several defenders.
commonErrors.correction: Protect possession and release to outside support.

commonErrors.error: Small forwards crowd the key forward’s feet.
commonErrors.correction: Hold outside positions and arrive after the spill.

commonErrors.error: The handball is delivered behind the runner.
commonErrors.correction: Lead the small forward into scoring space.

commonErrors.error: The key forward stops after disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Shepherd, block legally or remain available.

commonErrors.error: Forwards stop working after defenders win possession.
commonErrors.correction: Apply immediate pressure and protect the central exit.

progressions: Allow the aerial contest to be fully live.
Add another ground-level defender.
Permit match-like tackling.
Allow the key forward to finish when space opens.
Add scoreboard scenarios.
Continue into a front-half pressure game.
successIndicators: Recover immediately after the aerial contest.
Release accurately to a smaller forward.
matchApplication: Key forwards do not complete every marking opportunity. Their ability to recover, protect the spill and release to smaller teammates can turn an incomplete aerial contest into a scoring opportunity.

title: Goal-Line Ground-Ball Scramble
primarySkill: Defending and resolving a loose-football scramble immediately in front of goal
objective: Develop the ability of defenders to protect the goal line, organise roles and either secure, clear or safely neutralise a loose football during a high-pressure goal-square scramble.
groundSize: Goal square and an area extending approximately fifteen metres from goal.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert
setup:
Position three defenders and three forwards around the goal square.
Place one support player from each team outside the immediate contest.
Mark two defensive exit gates on either side of the goal square.
The coach begins each phase with a rolling, bouncing, spoiled or deflected football inside the scoring area.
Defenders must maintain at least one player between the football and goal.
Forwards attempt to gain possession and score.
Match-like legal contact is permitted for appropriately prepared players.
Rotate players through last-line, support and pressure roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach introduces the football into the goal-square area.
Defenders immediately organise goal-side, ball-pressure and outlet roles.
Forwards attack the loose football and attempt to create a scoring action.
The nearest defender contests the football.
A second defender protects the goal line.
The third defender provides an exit or support option.
If the defence wins possession, it attempts to exit through either gate.
If clean possession is unavailable, defenders may legally knock the football towards safety or create a controlled stoppage.
Forwards apply repeat pressure until possession exits, a score occurs or the coach stops play.
The group resets with a different initial spill.
coachingPoints: Protect the goal line before chasing the football.
Allocate one defender to the ball and one to dangerous space.
Avoid all defenders diving into the same contest.
Secure possession when cleanly available.
Use the boundary side or outside support when central exits are unsafe.
Do not handball blindly across the face of goal.
Maintain legal contact around players over the football.
Continue defending after the first clearance attempt.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether defenders organise immediately.
Whether the goal line remains protected.
Whether only the required players enter the contest.
Whether clean possession is taken when available.
Whether dangerous central disposal is avoided.
Whether forwards sustain legal pressure.
Whether defenders communicate the safest exit.
Whether repeat efforts continue after spills and smothers.

commonErrors.error: Every defender attacks the football and leaves goal exposed.
commonErrors.correction: Allocate one ball-pressure player and retain goal-line cover.

commonErrors.error: The ball winner handballs blindly into central space.
commonErrors.correction: Confirm a clear receiver or use a safer outside exit.

commonErrors.error: Defenders knock away a football that could be secured.
commonErrors.correction: Take clean possession when balanced and protected.

commonErrors.error: Players dive head-first into a crowded goal-square contest.
commonErrors.correction: Stay balanced, protect the head and enter from a safer angle.

commonErrors.error: Forwards stop after the first failed scoring attempt.
commonErrors.correction: Apply immediate repeat pressure and remain goal side of exits.

commonErrors.error: Defenders celebrate the clearance before possession is safe.
commonErrors.correction: Continue supporting until the football leaves the defensive area.

progressions: Add another forward.
Begin from a live marking contest.
Apply scoreboard and time scenarios.
Remove marked defensive exit gates.
Continue into a full defensive rebound.
Restart immediately after a behind.
regressions: Begin with two defenders and two forwards.
Stop after the first clean defensive possession.
successIndicators: Win or neutralise dangerous ground balls.
matchApplication: Loose footballs near the goal line create immediate scoring danger. Defenders must protect the line, remain composed and resolve the contest without every player being drawn towards the football.

title: Boundary Throw-In Ground-Ball Escape
primarySkill: Extracting a ground ball from a boundary throw-in contest
objective: Develop the ability to organise inside and outside roles at a boundary stoppage, win the resulting ground ball and move possession away from the boundary congestion.
groundSize: Boundary-side stoppage area approximately twenty-five metres long and twenty metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert
setup:
Position two rucks and two inside players from each team near the boundary.
Place one outside player from each team inboard of the contest.
Mark two inboard outlet gates and one down-the-line gate.
The coach conducts a controlled boundary throw-in or simulated tap.
Inside players compete for the resulting ground ball.
Outside players must remain clear of the initial congestion.
Teams attack opposite directions along the boundary line.
Rotate ruck, inside and outside roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach initiates the boundary throw-in.
Rucks compete and direct the football towards the stoppage area.
Inside players compete for the ground ball.
Outside players adjust according to the tap and defensive positioning.
The ball winner secures and protects possession.
The player selects an inboard, down-the-line or retention exit.
Outside support receives beyond the immediate tackle zone.
The possession team attempts to carry or dispose through a scoring gate.
If possession changes, teams reverse roles immediately.
The phase resets after an exit, turnover or secondary stoppage.
coachingPoints: Recognise the reduced space created by the boundary.
Maintain at least one inboard outlet.
Inside players should not all chase the same tap line.
Secure possession before attempting the release.
Avoid blind handballs towards the boundary line.
Use the down-the-line option only when it gains territory safely.
Outside support should receive facing the field.
Transition immediately after possession changes.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players organise around the boundary restriction.
Whether outside support remains inboard.
Whether the ground ball is secured.
Whether the first disposal leaves congestion.
Whether the receiver faces forward.
Whether the boundary is used safely.
Whether defenders protect central space.
Whether repeat efforts continue after secondary spills.

commonErrors.error: All players stand on the boundary side of the contest.
commonErrors.correction: Preserve an inboard receiver and central defensive cover.

commonErrors.error: The ball winner handballs towards the line without a target.
commonErrors.correction: Confirm the receiver or retain possession.

commonErrors.error: Outside players move into the initial stoppage.
commonErrors.correction: Hold beyond congestion until possession is established.

commonErrors.error: The down-the-line disposal is used despite heavy numbers.
commonErrors.correction: Use the inboard or rear option when the boundary route is blocked.

commonErrors.error: The receiver collects while facing the boundary.
commonErrors.correction: Adjust the starting angle to receive facing the field.

commonErrors.error: Players stop when the first extraction fails.
commonErrors.correction: Reorganise around the secondary ground-ball contest.

progressions: Remove marked outlet gates.
Add another outside player per team.
Allow full match-like tackling.
Apply scoreboard and time scenarios.
Continue into full-ground transition.
Vary the throw-in location.
regressions: Simulate the tap with a coach roll.
successIndicators: Organise effectively at the boundary stoppage.
Secure or neutralise the ground ball.
matchApplication: Boundary throw-ins compress numbers and limit available space. Effective teams maintain an inboard outlet and avoid allowing every player to become trapped between the football and boundary.

title: Forward 50 Repeat-Entry Ground-Ball Scenario
primarySkill: Winning a forward-50 ground ball and creating a repeat scoring entry
objective: Develop the ability to retain front-half possession after a spilled or intercepted entry and create a second, higher-quality scoring opportunity.
groundSize: Forward 50 and an area extending approximately twenty metres beyond the arc.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert
setup:
Position forwards and defenders inside 50.
Place attacking midfielders outside the contest as front-half support.
Begin each phase with an inside-50 kick designed to be spoiled, intercepted incompletely or brought to ground.
Mark two defensive rebound gates.
Mark reset and re-entry gates for the attacking team.
The attacking team attempts to win the ground ball and create another entry.
Defenders attempt to exit the area.
Rotate forwards, defenders and midfield support roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach or midfielder delivers the initial inside-50 kick.
Defenders and forwards contest the entry.
The football is brought to ground.
The nearest attacker competes for possession.
Teammates protect likely defensive exits and provide support behind.
If the attacking team wins possession, it may finish immediately or reset outside the contest.
Forwards reorganise their leading patterns.
The football is re-entered through the best available gate.
If defenders gain possession, they attempt to exit through a rebound gate.
Play continues until a score, clean defensive exit or coach reset.
coachingPoints: One player attacks the ground ball while others protect rebound space.
Do not crowd the football with every forward.
Secure possession before attempting a repeat entry.
Use support behind when the immediate scoring lane is closed.
Forwards must reset and separate before the second entry.
Protect the corridor after losing possession.
Reward repeat pressure as well as scoring outcome.
Maintain defensive balance outside the contest.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether attackers divide ball-winning and lock-in roles.
Whether the ground ball is secured.
Whether support remains outside congestion.
Whether defensive exits are protected.
Whether the attacking team recognises when to reset.
Whether forwards reorganise before re-entry.
Whether the second entry improves scoring probability.
Whether defenders transition cleanly when they win possession.

commonErrors.error: All forwards collapse onto the ground ball.
commonErrors.correction: Allocate one primary contestant and preserve outside pressure roles.

commonErrors.error: The ball winner attempts a blind shot under pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession and use the reset when the scoring lane is closed.

commonErrors.error: Supporting midfielders move too close.
commonErrors.correction: Hold outside the contest and provide a clear re-entry platform.

commonErrors.error: Forwards continue old leads during the reset.
commonErrors.correction: Stop, separate and organise new leading patterns.

commonErrors.error: The attacking team protects the boundary but leaves the corridor open.
commonErrors.correction: Close the most dangerous central rebound first.

commonErrors.error: Players judge success only by whether a goal is scored.
commonErrors.correction: Assess ground-ball win, lock-in and quality of repeat entry.

progressions: Add another defender.
Remove marked reset gates.
Allow match-like tackling.
Add scoreboard and time pressure.
Continue play after behinds.
Begin from different inside-50 entry angles.
regressions: Stop after the first repeat possession.
successIndicators: Win or neutralise the forward-50 ground ball.
matchApplication: Repeat entries are often created by winning the ground ball after an incomplete forward entry. Teams must retain structure around the contest rather than sending every forward directly to the football.
relatedDrills: GB-067 – Half-Forward Ground-Ball Reset and Re-Entry

title: Wet-Weather Ground-Ball Territory Game
primarySkill: Winning ground-ball territory and retaining structure in wet conditions
objective: Develop team behaviours suited to wet conditions, including secure collection, territorial decision making, repeat contests and simplified disposal.
groundSize: Rectangle approximately fifty metres long and thirty-five metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert
setup:
Divide players into two teams.
Mark a scoring zone at each end.
Lightly wet the footballs while ensuring the playing surface remains safe.
Begin every phase with a rolling, bouncing or skidding football.
Teams score by carrying possession into the end zone or gaining controlled territory through a designated gate.
Award bonus points for clean wet-weather collection and repeat ground-ball wins.
Controlled tackling is permitted.
Stop immediately if the surface becomes unsafe.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach introduces a wet football into the playing area.
Teams compete for possession.
The ball winner attempts to secure the football with two hands.
Teammates provide support behind and outside the contest.
The possession team selects a simple disposal or territorial option.
If possession spills, players complete an immediate second effort.
The defending team protects central space and applies pressure.
A team scores by reaching the end zone or completing the nominated territorial action.
A new wet ground ball is introduced after each score or stoppage.
Play continues for timed blocks with surface and football checks between blocks.
coachingPoints: Adjust approach speed for the skidding football.
Use soft hands and absorb the football into the body.
Expect fumbles and remain ready for a second effort.
Use simple handballs and lower-risk kicks.
Gain territory when clean possession cannot be maintained.
Maintain players behind the football.
Avoid overhandling in congestion.
Place player safety above drill intensity.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players adjust approach speed.
Whether two-hand collection is prioritised.
Whether the football is absorbed into the body.
Whether second efforts occur immediately.
Whether disposal choices suit the conditions.
Whether support remains behind possession.
Whether teams gain useful territory.
Whether footing and contact remain safe.

commonErrors.error: Players approach the skidding football at uncontrolled speed.
commonErrors.correction: Slow earlier and shorten the final steps.

commonErrors.error: The ball winner attempts intricate disposal in congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Use the simplest effective option.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after a fumble.
commonErrors.correction: Expect the spill and complete the next effort immediately.

commonErrors.error: Teams handball repeatedly without escaping pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Use territory or an outside exit when congestion remains.

commonErrors.error: All players move ahead of the football.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain support and defensive protection behind possession.

commonErrors.error: The drill continues despite unsafe footing.
commonErrors.correction: Stop, inspect the surface and modify or end the activity.

progressions: Increase pressure within safe limits.
Remove marked territorial gates.
Add scoreboard and time scenarios.
Continue into a larger match simulation.
Use more irregular ground-ball feeds.
Restrict the number of handballs before a territorial action.
matchApplication: Wet-weather football produces more ground-ball contests and fewer clean possession chains. Teams must simplify disposal, expect repeated spills and value territory without abandoning support structure.

title: Match Ground-Ball Audit Game
primarySkill: Auditing team ground-ball behaviour during extended match simulation
objective: Evaluate how consistently the team applies its ground-ball principles during realistic, extended and minimally interrupted match play.
groundSize: Full oval or three-quarter oval.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert
setup:
Divide players into two balanced teams.
Use realistic positional structures and interchange.
Play timed match-simulation blocks.
Coaches record ground-ball behaviours without stopping play except for safety.
Restart normal stoppages using centre bounces, boundary throw-ins, ball-ups or realistic loose-football feeds.
Assign observers to technical, structural, transition and positional categories.
Use scoreboard conditions appropriate to the training phase.
Review observations only between blocks.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins under normal Australian football rules.
Coaches record every significant ground-ball contest.
Observers identify which team wins first possession.
They record whether the ball winner secures, protects and disposes effectively.
Team structure around the contest is assessed.
Transition after possession gain or loss is recorded.
Positional responsibilities are assessed according to field location.
Play continues with minimal coach interruption.
Teams receive brief evidence-based feedback between blocks.
A final block tests whether identified behaviours improve.
coachingPoints: Avoid coaching every individual contest during play.
Observe what players do without immediate instruction.
Record both possession result and process.
Assess numbers inside and outside the contest.
Record support behind the football.
Evaluate the first disposal after the win.
Assess defensive reaction after loss.
Compare behaviour across different field positions.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Contest entry and safety.
Clean collection percentage.
Ball protection after possession.
Number of players entering the contest.
Outside and rear support.
First-disposal effectiveness.
Repeat efforts after spills.
Positional decision making.
Communication.
Transition after possession changes.
Performance under fatigue.
Improvement between blocks.

commonErrors.error: Coaches interrupt too often to correct errors.
commonErrors.correction: Record patterns and provide feedback between blocks.

commonErrors.error: Observers record only who wins the football.
commonErrors.correction: Assess collection, support, disposal and transition.

commonErrors.error: Different observers use inconsistent standards.
commonErrors.correction: Agree on definitions and scoring criteria before play.

commonErrors.error: Players alter behaviour because every contest is verbally assessed.
commonErrors.correction: Keep observation discreet and allow realistic play.

commonErrors.error: Feedback is too broad to guide improvement.
commonErrors.correction: Use specific examples and measurable patterns.

commonErrors.error: The final block repeats the same errors without a focus.
commonErrors.correction: Give each line one or two clear behavioural targets.

progressions: Use full match duration blocks.
Add external umpires.
Restrict coach communication completely.
Use live video review.
Apply complex scoreboard scenarios.
Compare results with competition footage.
regressions: Assess only two or three ground-ball behaviours.
Stop once per block for guided correction.
matchApplication: Extended match simulation reveals whether ground-ball behaviours remain reliable when players are fatigued, under scoreboard pressure and required to organise without constant coach intervention.

title: Ground-Ball Chapter Final Assessment
primarySkill: Completing a comprehensive assessment of individual and team ground-ball performance
objective: Provide a final structured assessment covering the complete Ground Balls chapter, from fundamental collection through movement, pressure, team structure, advanced decisions and match application.
groundSize: Six assessment stations across half an oval, followed by a three-quarter or full-ground assessment game.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert
setup:
Establish six assessment stations:
Station 1: Fundamental collection and body position.
Station 2: Moving pickup, exit and disposal.
Station 3: Pressure, contact and second effort.
Station 4: Team outlet and transition structure.
Station 5: Advanced decision and risk selection.
Station 6: Position-specific match scenario.
Scale contact, distance and complexity according to age and ability.
Assign trained observers to every station.
Provide one familiarisation repetition before scoring.
Finish with an extended match-simulation audit game.
Score individual technique and team performance separately.
Standardise feeds, pressure and criteria.
Schedule recovery between high-load stations.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players rotate through all six assessment stations.
Each player completes three scored repetitions at every station.
Coaches assess the complete action before, during and after possession.
No technical coaching is given during scored repetitions.
Individual scores cover collection, balance, protection, scanning, decision and disposal.
Team scores cover role allocation, support, communication and transition.
After station assessment, players complete timed match-simulation blocks.
Every significant ground-ball contest is audited during the game.
Results from stations and match simulation are compared.
Coaches produce individual and team development priorities from the combined assessment.
coachingPoints: Use age-appropriate contact and complexity.
Assess technical fundamentals before tactical outcome.
Record whether the player reaches the correct football line.
Evaluate movement and balance after collection.
Assess performance under pressure and contact.
Record support recognition and disposal choice.
Evaluate team organisation around the contest.
Compare controlled-station performance with match transfer.
Record strengths as well as deficiencies.
Stop any activity where fatigue compromises safety.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Approach line and speed.
Body position at collection.
Two-hand security.
Balance and momentum.
Ball protection.
Pre-collection and post-collection scanning.
Decision making under pressure.
Disposal legality and effectiveness.
Second effort.
Inside and outside role organisation.
Support behind possession.
Communication.
Positional responsibility.
Transition after possession change.
Technical transfer into match simulation.

commonErrors.error: Assessment conditions vary significantly between groups.
commonErrors.correction: Standardise feeds, space, contact and scoring before beginning.

commonErrors.error: Coaches assess only the final possession outcome.
commonErrors.correction: Score the complete process from approach through transition.

commonErrors.error: Players receive coaching during scored repetitions.
commonErrors.correction: Record the issue and provide feedback after assessment.

commonErrors.error: Technical and tactical errors are combined into one score.
commonErrors.correction: Record collection, decision and execution separately.

commonErrors.error: Match-simulation observations are not linked to station results.
commonErrors.correction: Compare controlled performance with live-game transfer.

commonErrors.error: Fatigue invalidates later results.
commonErrors.correction: Balance station order and provide sufficient recovery.

commonErrors.error: Younger or developing players face excessive complexity.
commonErrors.correction: Scale contact, numbers, distances and decisions appropriately.

commonErrors.error: Feedback identifies weaknesses without development priorities.
commonErrors.correction: Convert results into specific technical and team training targets.

progressions: Repeat under wet conditions where safe.
Add more complex scoreboard situations.
Remove marked gates and visual cues.
Include external match officials.
Compare results with competition statistics and video.
Repeat the assessment at defined seasonal checkpoints.
regressions: Assess four stations rather than six.
Separate technical and tactical assessment across different sessions.
successIndicators: Transfer station performance into match play.
matchApplication: The final assessment determines whether players can transfer the complete ground-ball skill set into realistic Australian football. It identifies technical, tactical, physical and team-structure priorities for future training.
relatedDrills: GB-060 – Ground-Ball Pressure and Contest Assessment

title: Stationary Handball Fundamentals
primarySkill: Basic stationary handball technique
objective: Develop a repeatable stationary handball action in which players correctly support the football, strike its lower rear section with a closed fist and direct it towards a controlled target.
groundSize: A flat 10-metre × 10-metre technical area, or one clearly marked station for every two to four players.
equipment: Flat markers or small target cones
Optional handball technique boards or rebound nets
coachingDifficulty: 1 – Simple organisation and observation
setup:
Mark a safe technical area with adequate spacing between players.
Each player stands with a football and at least two metres of clear space around them.
Players face a cone, line marking, partner or stationary target positioned three to five metres away.
Begin without speed, competition or defensive pressure.
Right-handed players initially place their left foot slightly forward when handballing with the right fist; reverse the stance for the opposite hand.
The coach positions themselves where the support hand, striking fist and ball contact point can be clearly observed.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players begin in an athletic stance with knees slightly flexed, head up and the football supported in front of the body.
On the coach’s instruction, each player forms a compact striking fist with the thumb positioned outside the fingers.
Players place the football on the open supporting hand with the long axis directed towards the target.
The striking fist moves forward from behind the football and contacts its lower rear section.
The supporting hand remains open and stable while the striking arm follows through towards the target.
Players retrieve the football, reset their body position and repeat the action at a controlled tempo.
Complete sets of six to ten repetitions before changing the striking hand.
The coach pauses the group when necessary to demonstrate or correct a common technical fault.
coachingPoints: Hold the football on the open supporting hand rather than gripping it tightly between both hands.
Keep the football in front of the body where the player can see the ball and the intended target.
Form a firm, compact fist with the wrist straight and the thumb safely outside the fingers.
Strike through the lower rear section of the football rather than pushing or carrying it forward.
Keep the supporting hand stable and avoid throwing the football upwards before contact.
Transfer body weight slightly towards the target as the fist moves through the ball.
Finish with the striking fist pointing towards the target.
Prioritise clean contact and legal technique before speed or distance.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players begin with a balanced stance and the football positioned in front of the body.
Whether the supporting hand stays open and underneath the football.
Whether the fist contacts the football rather than the supporting hand.
Whether the football leaves the hand from a clear striking action rather than a throw.
Whether the follow-through travels towards the intended target.
Whether players can repeat the technique without rushing or losing body control.

commonErrors.error: The football is tossed or thrown from the supporting hand.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the supporting hand still and require the fist to create the football’s movement.

commonErrors.error: The fist contacts the side or middle of the football.
commonErrors.correction: Mark or point to the lower rear contact area and slow the action until contact improves.

commonErrors.error: The striking wrist bends on impact.
commonErrors.correction: Form a firmer fist and keep the wrist aligned with the forearm.

commonErrors.error: The player grips the football tightly with both hands.
commonErrors.correction: Rest the football on the open supporting palm with only light finger control.

commonErrors.error: The player stands upright with locked knees.
commonErrors.correction: Adopt a balanced athletic stance with soft knees and a slight forward weight transfer.

commonErrors.error: The follow-through finishes across the body.
commonErrors.correction: Direct the fist straight through the football and towards the target.

progressions: Handball towards a partner or stationary target from four to six metres.
Complete consecutive repetitions without pausing between each handball.
Alternate the striking hand after every repetition.
Require players to nominate the target before beginning the action.
regressions: Practise the fist movement without a football.
Hold the football closer to the striking fist to reduce the length of the action.
Use a larger soft football or reduced distance for younger players.
Allow the coach or partner to hold the football lightly while the player practises clean contact.
successIndicators: Support the football on an open and stable hand.
Make clear fist-to-football contact without throwing the ball.
Direct the football towards the intended target.
Demonstrate the basic action with both hands at a controlled speed.
matchApplication: A legal and technically sound handball is the foundation of releasing a teammate, maintaining possession and moving the football through congestion. Players who establish correct supporting-hand position, contact and follow-through are better prepared to execute under movement and pressure later in the chapter.

title: Contact Point and Follow-Through
primarySkill: Clean striking contact and directional follow-through
objective: Develop clean contact on the lower rear section of the football and a straight follow-through that produces controlled, accurate ball flight.
groundSize: Pairs positioned four metres apart within a 15-metre × 15-metre technical area.
equipment: Optional removable ball markers or tape
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge and one main teaching focus
setup:
Organise players in pairs facing each other four metres apart.
Place one cone beside each player to maintain the correct distance.
One player begins with the football while the partner presents both hands as a target.
Players use a controlled stationary stance.
The coach identifies the lower rear striking area of the football before the drill begins.
Pairs complete separate blocks with the right and left fist.
howTheDrillWorks:
The player with the football establishes a stable support-hand platform.
The player forms a closed fist with a straight wrist and positions it behind the football.
The fist travels directly through the lower rear section of the football.
The player completes the action with the fist pointing towards the partner’s chest.
The receiver secures the football, briefly checks the previous handball’s flight and returns it using the same technique.
Partners complete eight handballs each with one fist.
Players then change the supporting and striking hands for a second set.
The pair counts clean handballs that travel directly to the partner without excessive loop, wobble or sideways rotation.
coachingPoints: Keep the striking fist compact, with the thumb outside the fingers.
Align the wrist with the forearm before and during contact.
Contact the lower rear section of the football to produce forward flight.
Drive through the football rather than stopping the fist at impact.
Follow through directly towards the partner’s chest.
Use a small forward weight transfer rather than leaning backwards.
Maintain a stable supporting hand until the football has left the platform.
Judge quality by clean flight and accuracy, not by how hard the football is struck.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the fist is correctly formed before the action begins.
Whether the wrist remains straight at the point of contact.
Whether contact occurs on the football rather than the support hand.
Whether the football travels with controlled forward rotation rather than excessive wobble.
Whether the follow-through finishes towards the partner.
Whether players maintain the same mechanics with both fists.

commonErrors.error: The fist strikes the middle or top of the football.
commonErrors.correction: Lower the contact point and rehearse the fist path slowly.

commonErrors.error: The wrist bends or turns at impact.
commonErrors.correction: Reset the fist and align the wrist directly behind the football.

commonErrors.error: The action stops immediately after contact.
commonErrors.correction: Extend the fist towards the partner and complete the follow-through.

commonErrors.error: The football floats excessively upwards.
commonErrors.correction: Strike through the lower rear rather than underneath the ball.

commonErrors.error: The football travels across the partner’s body.
commonErrors.correction: Align the platform, fist path and follow-through with the centre of the target.

commonErrors.error: The player tries to create power only with the arm.
commonErrors.correction: Add a controlled weight transfer towards the target.

progressions: Increase the partner distance to five or six metres.
Handball through a one-metre-wide cone gate before reaching the receiver.
Complete five consecutive accurate handballs without resetting the count.
Alternate hands after every handball.
regressions: Reduce the distance to two or three metres.
Use a larger chest-level target such as a handball board.
Pause with the fist positioned behind the football before striking.
Practise the follow-through without a football.
successIndicators: Contact the lower rear section of the football.
Produce controlled and direct ball flight.
Perform the action effectively with both fists.
matchApplication: Clean contact and directional follow-through allow players to release teammates accurately at short and medium distances. This is essential when handballing through congestion, feeding a runner or maintaining possession after winning the football at ground level.

title: Receive at Speed and Release Forward
Boundary Throw-In Fold-Out Handball
primarySkill: Using layered support to exit a boundary throw-in
objective: Develop a boundary-stoppage exit in which midfielders fold away from the contest and use handball to move the football from the boundary into open space.
groundSize: A boundary stoppage area approximately 20 metres × 18 metres with an inside exit lane.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert stoppage structure and contact management
setup:
Mark a boundary line and stoppage zone.
Position one first-possession player near the boundary side of the contest.
Place one fold-out support player two to three metres inside.
Position one wider release runner further infield.
Add two controlled-pressure opponents.
Place a finishing receiver 15 metres infield.
The coach feeds the football from a boundary throw-in simulation.
Mirror the activity on both boundaries.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach throws or feeds the football into the stoppage.
The first-possession player secures the football near the boundary.
The fold-out support player moves laterally and slightly backwards into clear space.

Whether the football exits the stoppage in possession.
Whether the pattern works from both boundaries.

The first handball must be short and accurate.
The original ball carrier should fold behind before moving outside.
Player B should engage the defender before returning the football.
The return handball must lead Player A into the outside lane.
Running lines should remain clearly separated.
Use the correct hand for each direction.
Continue forward after breaking the pressure line.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether Player B times the inside support run.
Whether Player A folds behind rather than crossing in front.
Whether Player B draws the defender.
Whether the return handball leads the outside runner.
Whether players maintain separate lanes.
Whether the final connection remains accurate.
Whether both wings are used effectively.

Reduce channel width.
Introduce controlled tackling.
Finish with a forward entry.

matchApplication: Wing players can use an inside teammate to draw pressure and regain possession outside. The fold-and-return pattern creates overlap while maintaining width and forward momentum.

setup:
Organise groups of four: feeder, receiver-ball carrier and two support players.

Before the feed, only one support player moves into the active lane.
The receiver must scan over both shoulders before the football arrives.
One shadow defender may stand in front to restrict prolonged turning.
Rotate roles regularly.
howTheDrillWorks:
Both support players begin in their starting positions.
The receiver scans over each shoulder.
One support player moves into space and calls.
The feeder delivers the football to the receiver.
The receiver secures possession while facing the feeder.
Using the earlier scan and communication, the receiver organises the football and handballs to the active support player.

Confirm the support player’s movement and voice.
Secure the football cleanly before release.

Whether the handball is accurate.

Whether non-dominant-side releases remain controlled.

title: Elite Handball Decision and Execution Assessment

coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert workload, stoppage and contact management
setup:
Divide players into two midfield groups.
Mark a central stoppage circle and two exit corridors.
Begin with a live or controlled ball-up.
Each repetition lasts until a clean exit or turnover.
Players immediately complete a short recovery run and return for the next stoppage.
Roles rotate between first possession, close support, outside release and pressure.
Work in blocks of four to six stoppages.
Provide planned recovery between blocks.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach initiates the first stoppage.
Players contest for possession.

The opposition applies match-like pressure.

Teams immediately reorganise for the next stoppage.

Record successful exits, illegal disposals and role errors.
Provide recovery and one technical correction.
Repeat the block with changed roles or exit conditions.
coachingPoints: Re-establish roles before every stoppage.
Fatigue must not remove first-, second- and third-possession structure.
Protect the football before releasing.
Use short, direct handballs in congestion.
Outside support must continue to hold width.
Maintain legal technique when breathing and heart rate are elevated.
Recovery running should not prevent safe contest preparation.
End the block if technique or contact standards deteriorate.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether roles are reorganised between repetitions.
Whether technical accuracy declines.
Whether players default to the dominant-hand side.
Whether outside support collapses.
Whether illegal disposal increases.
Whether physical movement remains safe.
Whether players apply the correction in the next block.

commonErrors.error: Players fail to reorganise before the next stoppage.
commonErrors.correction: Assign roles during the recovery run.

commonErrors.error: Handballs become throws under fatigue.
commonErrors.correction: Stop the block and restore the legal support platform and strike.

commonErrors.error: All players move towards the contest.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain outside and behind-ball roles.

commonErrors.error: First-possession players release without protecting the football.
commonErrors.correction: Secure and position the body before disposal.

commonErrors.error: Recovery running creates unsafe contact preparation.

title: Kick-In Play-On Handball Escape

groundSize: A defensive goal-square and kick-in area approximately 30 metres long and 25 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert kick-in, field-position and pressure management
setup:
Position the kick-in player inside the goal square.
Place one short support player towards the boundary pocket.
Position one player behind and outside the initial support.
Place one wider receiver beyond the first pressure line.
Add two defenders who guard the short kick and begin closing once the kick-in player plays on.
Mark a prohibited central turnover zone.
The kick-in player must clearly leave the goal square before handballing.
Mirror the structure on both sides of the ground.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach signals that the kick-in may begin.
The kick-in player scans the short kicking options and defensive structure.

Maintain support behind the football after the first release.
Do not use the handball option when the short kick or safe long kick is clearly superior.

Whether the player legally exits the goal square.
Whether short support appears at a safe angle.
Whether the first handball avoids the dangerous central zone.
Whether the receiver is protected through placement.
Whether support behind remains connected.
Whether players recognise when handball is not the best option.

The first defender begins the planned switch with a short handball.

Nearby support should separate rather than crowd the contest.

Protect receivers through accurate placement.
Maintain urgency without forcing a low-quality possession.

Mark two possession grids:

commonErrors.correction: Clear space when the current ball carrier has the better forward option.

commonErrors.error: The group loses support behind after multiple handballs.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain one emergency option beneath possession.

commonErrors.error: Players judge success only by completing handballs.
commonErrors.correction: Evaluate the quality of the final forward connection.

progressions: Increase defensive numbers.
Reduce the size of the kicking zones.
Add scoreboard and time scenarios.
Allow full match-like contact.
Use live forward leading patterns.
regressions: Limit the chain to a fixed number of handballs.
successIndicators: Recognise the correct moment to kick.
Deliver the final disposal from balance.
Connect effectively with the forward target.
matchApplication: Handball chains should finish once they create a player with time, balance and a useful kicking lane. Continuing to handball after that moment can allow defenders to recover and increase turnover risk.
relatedDrills: HB-086 – Overlap or Hold Decision Game

title: Player-Led Handball Scenario Challenge
primarySkill: Designing and executing a player-led handball solution to an unknown match scenario
objective: Assess and develop the players’ ability to interpret a match scenario, create an appropriate handball plan and execute it with minimal coach intervention.
groundSize: Half to full ground, depending on the selected scenario.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert facilitation and performance-review management
setup:
Divide players into two teams.
Select leaders or captains for each team.
Give each team a scenario card without prescribing the solution.
Example scenarios include:
Defensive possession against a full-ground press.
Centre stoppage while trailing late.
Boundary possession while protecting a lead.
Temporary numerical disadvantage.
Forward-half turnover with limited time.
Allow players a short planning period.
Coaches observe but do not design the plan.
Use normal match rules and contact.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach provides the scenario and relevant score, time and field position.
Team leaders organise roles and communicate the handball plan.
Players position themselves for the restart.
The scenario begins under match-like pressure.
Teams execute their chosen strategy.
The coach records decisions, structure and communication without stopping play.
The scenario ends after a score, exit, turnover or time expiry.
Players conduct a short review of what worked and what failed.
The team modifies one element of the plan.
The scenario is repeated or reversed.
coachingPoints: Players must identify the actual problem before designing the solution.
Roles should be clear but adaptable.
The plan should include support inside, outside or behind as required.
Handball must serve the scenario rather than become the objective.
Leaders should communicate score, time and risk.
Players must adjust when the opposition disrupts the plan.
Reviews should focus on observable decisions and movement.
Coaches should guide reflection without supplying every answer.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players understand the scenario.
Whether leaders allocate useful roles.
Whether the plan reflects score, time and field position.
Whether support structure appears before possession.
Whether players adapt when the plan is disrupted.
Whether handball decisions are purposeful.
Whether the review identifies specific improvements.

commonErrors.error: Players begin planning before agreeing on the scenario problem.
commonErrors.correction: Define the score, time, field position and opposition threat first.

commonErrors.error: The plan contains too many fixed handballs.
commonErrors.correction: Build principles and roles rather than a rigid disposal sequence.

commonErrors.error: Only the leaders understand the plan.
commonErrors.correction: Require players to repeat their role before beginning.

commonErrors.error: The team continues the plan after the opposition closes it.
commonErrors.correction: Use agreed contingency and reset options.

commonErrors.error: The review focuses only on the outcome.
commonErrors.correction: Discuss the information, decision and movement that produced the outcome.

commonErrors.error: Players rely on the coach to solve the scenario.
commonErrors.correction: Return responsibility to the team leaders and supporting players.

progressions: Reduce planning time.
Provide incomplete or changing scenario information.
Allow the opposition to design a counter-strategy.
Add player-led video review.
Change the scenario during play.
regressions: Give teams a list of possible principles.
Limit the scenario to half ground.
Allow one coach question during planning.
Rehearse the first movement before live play.
successIndicators: Apply one specific improvement in the repeat.
matchApplication: Players must solve match problems on the field without constant coach direction. Leadership, shared understanding and adaptable handball principles allow teams to respond effectively to changing scenarios.

title: Complete Handball Chapter Assessment
primarySkill: Assessing complete handball competency from fundamental technique to match application
objective: Conduct a complete final assessment of each player’s handball technique, movement, pressure execution, team use, advanced decision making and match-scenario application.
skillLevel: Foundation to Elite, with assessment standards adjusted to the playing group
groundSize: Six assessment stations arranged across half to full ground.
contact: 3 – Match-Like Contact, adjusted appropriately for age and competition level
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert whole-chapter assessment and feedback management
setup:
Establish six assessment stations:
Station 1 – Fundamental Technique: Stationary dominant- and non-dominant-hand accuracy.
Station 2 – Movement: Receive, run and release to moving targets.
Station 3 – Pressure: Protected-side handball under shadow and controlled contact.
Station 4 – Team Use: Inside, outside and behind-ball support within a possession chain.
Station 5 – Advanced Decision Making: Deception, defender engagement, receiver protection and risk selection.
Station 6 – Match Scenario: Full-team scenario involving score, time, field position and turnover transition.
Divide players evenly between stations.
Assign coaches or trained observers.
Explain assessment standards and contact restrictions.
Allow one brief practice repetition at Stations 1–5.
Schedule sufficient recovery before Station 6.
Record dominant- and non-dominant-side performance separately.
howTheDrillWorks:
At Station 1, players complete five dominant-hand and five non-dominant-hand target handballs.
At Station 2, players complete moving receive-and-release tasks to both sides.
At Station 3, players complete protected releases against closing and controlled contact pressure.
At Station 4, players perform as ball carrier, inside support, outside support and behind-ball support.
At Station 5, players complete live decisions involving deception, numerical advantage and receiver protection.
At Station 6, teams complete one or more match scenarios under realistic pressure.
Coaches score technique, legality, accuracy, balance, scanning, decision quality, support and match impact.
Each player receives results across all six competency areas.
Players repeat one technical and one tactical task linked to their lowest scores.
Coaches retain the results to guide future programming and individual development.
coachingPoints: Apply the same legal handball standard throughout the assessment.
Adjust expectations for age, experience and competition level without changing the core skill requirements.
Assess both hands independently.
Judge movement skills by whether the player remains balanced and leads the receiver.
Assess pressure disposal by protection, legality and decision timing.
Include support before and after possession.
Judge advanced handballs by the advantage created, not by complexity.
Consider scoreboard, time, field position and turnover consequence in scenario scoring.
Record specific evidence rather than broad impressions.
Feedback should identify clear next training priorities.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players execute legal fundamental technique.
Whether both hands are functional.
Whether moving handballs preserve balance and receiver momentum.
Whether the football is protected under pressure.
Whether players scan before possession.
Whether support exists inside, outside and behind.
Whether advanced decisions create genuine advantage.
Whether players adjust risk to match context.
Whether turnover reactions are immediate.
Whether feedback is applied during repeated tasks.

commonErrors.error: The dominant hand masks a major non-dominant weakness.
commonErrors.correction: Record each side separately and prescribe specific opposite-hand work.

commonErrors.error: Moving handballs are accurate only after the player stops.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce speed and rebuild continuous movement through release.

commonErrors.error: Pressure causes the disposal to become a throw.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce pressure and restore the stable platform and clear fist strike.

commonErrors.error: Players judge handball quality only by completion.
commonErrors.correction: Consider receiver protection, momentum and next action.

commonErrors.error: Support arrives after the ball carrier is already pressured.
commonErrors.correction: Begin movement before possession is secured.

commonErrors.error: Advanced deception is used unnecessarily.
commonErrors.correction: Select the simplest disposal that creates advantage.

commonErrors.error: Players force possession because the assessment focuses on handballing.
commonErrors.correction: Handball only when it is the appropriate match decision.

commonErrors.error: Scenario decisions ignore score, time or field position.
commonErrors.correction: Confirm the full context before play begins.

progressions: Repeat the assessment later in the season under greater pressure.
Increase contact and decision complexity for advanced groups.
Compare positional and individual results.
Add video-supported player self-assessment.
Include opposition-specific tactical scenarios.
Convert results into individual development programs.
regressions: Assess each competency area on separate training nights.
Use controlled walkthroughs before live scenarios.
Reduce physical load for junior or returning players.
successIndicators: Execute legal handballs with both hands.
Adapt technique and risk to match scenarios.
Demonstrate measurable competency across all six assessment areas.
matchApplication: Complete handball performance combines sound technique, movement, pressure control, support structure, decision making and match awareness. This final assessment determines whether players can transfer the full handball chapter into realistic Australian football performance.
relatedDrills: HB-050 – Pressure and Contest Handball Assessment

title: Stationary Drop Punt
primarySkill: Drop Punt Technique
objective: Develop a technically sound stationary drop punt by teaching correct ball drop, body position, foot contact and follow-through before introducing movement or defensive pressure.
players:
Minimum: 2
Ideal: 10–20
Maximum: Unlimited (working in pairs)
groundSize:
Small Area
Approximately 20 m × 20 m
coachingDifficulty: 1 – Beginner Coach
setup:
Players work in pairs facing each other.
Players should stand:
Under 8–10: 8–10 metres apart.
Under 12–14: 10–15 metres apart.
Under 16 and above: 15–20 metres apart.
Spread pairs evenly across the training area to prevent footballs crossing into neighbouring groups.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A begins with the football.
Player A performs a stationary drop punt to Player B.
Player B marks or gathers the football.
Player B resets before returning the kick.
Continue for the nominated time.
Swap the preferred kicking foot after several minutes if appropriate.
Players should prioritise correct technique rather than kicking distance.
coachingPoints: Hold the football correctly.
Guide the ball onto the boot rather than throwing it.
Keep their head over the football.
Strike the ball with the laces of the boot.
Finish balanced.
Follow through directly towards the target.
Encourage smooth, controlled kicking rather than maximum power.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Ball drop consistency.
Body balance.
Foot-to-ball contact.
Accuracy.
Follow-through.
Confidence.
Consistency from kick to kick.
Provide one coaching correction before allowing several repetitions.

commonErrors.error: Throwing the ball onto the boot
commonErrors.correction: Guide the football gently from the hands.

commonErrors.error: Leaning backwards
commonErrors.correction: Keep the chest over the football.

commonErrors.error: Falling sideways
commonErrors.correction: Finish balanced on the kicking foot.

commonErrors.error: Looking at the target too early
commonErrors.correction: Watch the football until contact.

commonErrors.error: Swinging across the body
commonErrors.correction: Finish with the kicking leg pointing towards the target.

progressions: Increase kicking distance.
Introduce the non-preferred foot.
Reduce preparation time between kicks.
Introduce moving targets.
Progress to KK-002.
regressions: Allow players to stop and reset after every kick.
Slow the pace of the activity.
Demonstrate the technique again before restarting.
successIndicators: Maintain balance throughout the kicking action.
matchApplication:
The drop punt is the primary kicking technique used throughout Australian Football.
This drill develops the technical foundation required for:
Maintaining possession.
Passing to teammates.
Kicking inside 50.
Defensive exits.
Goal kicking.
General field kicking.
Every advanced kicking drill in the AFCRL builds upon the skills developed in KK-001.

title: Partner Accuracy Challenge
primarySkill: Passing Accuracy
objective: Develop the ability to consistently deliver the football to a teammate's advantage by improving kicking accuracy, control and judgement of kicking weight. Players learn that an effective pass is one that allows the receiver to mark or gather the football with minimal movement.
players:
Minimum: 2
Ideal: 10–20
Maximum: Unlimited (working in pairs)
groundSize:
Small Area
Approximately 20 m × 20 m
coachingDifficulty: 1 – Beginner Coach
setup:
Players work in pairs facing each other.
Players should stand:
Under 8–10: 8–10 metres apart.
Under 12–14: 10–15 metres apart.
Under 16 and above: 15–20 metres apart.
Each pair should have sufficient space to kick safely without interfering with neighbouring groups.
The receiving player should remain stationary throughout the drill.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A kicks to Player B.
The objective is to deliver the football directly to Player B's chest without requiring them to move their feet.
Player B marks or gathers the football.
Player B immediately returns the kick using the same objective.
Continue for the allocated time.
Coaches may introduce a simple scoring system:
2 points for a chest mark.
1 point if the receiver gathers the football cleanly after one bounce.
0 points if the receiver must move significantly or the football misses the target.
The emphasis should remain on quality rather than competition.
coachingPoints: Look at the target before beginning the kicking action.
Kick to where the receiver can comfortably mark the football.
Match the force of the kick to the required distance.
Maintain the same drop punt technique regardless of distance.
Stay balanced throughout the kicking action.
Finish towards the intended target.
Players should understand that kicking accurately is more important than kicking hard.
coachingCues: "Kick to your teammate, not at them."
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the receiver is forced to move.
Ball flight.
Accuracy.
Kicking weight.
Follow-through.
Body balance.
Consistency from kick to kick.
Encourage players to evaluate each kick before receiving coaching feedback.

commonErrors.error: Receiver moving sideways
commonErrors.correction: Finish directly towards the target.

commonErrors.error: Kick travelling too high
commonErrors.correction: Reduce the height of the ball drop and maintain a flatter trajectory.

commonErrors.error: Kick travelling too hard
commonErrors.correction: Reduce leg speed and focus on control.

commonErrors.error: Kick falling short
commonErrors.correction: Complete the follow-through and accelerate through the football.

commonErrors.error: Receiver unable to mark comfortably
commonErrors.correction: Encourage the kicker to visualise the exact landing point before kicking.

progressions: Increase kicking distance.
Use the non-preferred foot.
Introduce a moving receiver.
Reduce preparation time before kicking.
Progress to KK-004.
regressions: Encourage players to stop and reset after each kick.
successIndicators: Deliver the football directly to the receiver.
Require minimal movement from the receiver.
Demonstrate good judgement of kicking weight.
Improve accuracy over the duration of the drill.
matchApplication: Most possessions in Australian Football involve passing to a teammate under little or no pressure. This drill develops the fundamental ability to consistently hit a teammate's preferred side, allowing the next possession to be completed quickly and efficiently.

title: Kick and Follow
primarySkill: Kicking While Moving
objective: Teach players to move immediately after disposing of the football rather than remaining stationary. Players kick to a teammate, follow their kick and rotate continuously through the drill.
groundSize:
Small to Medium Area
Approximately 25 m × 15 m per group
coachingDifficulty: 1 – Beginner Coach
setup:
Create two lines facing each other.
Place one cone at the front of each line.
Recommended distance between lines:
Under 8–10: 10 metres.
Under 12–14: 15 metres.
Under 16 and above: 20 metres.
Place a second cone approximately three metres behind each front cone to organise the waiting players.
The football begins with the first player in one line.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A kicks to Player B at the opposite line.
Player A immediately follows the kick by running to the back of Player B’s line.
Player B marks or gathers the football.
Player B resets and kicks to the next player in the opposite line.
Player B follows the kick to the back of that line.
The drill continues in a continuous pattern.
Players should communicate the intended target before kicking.
coachingPoints: Prepare the football before reaching the kicking point.
Kick accurately to the receiver’s advantage.
Move immediately after disposal.
Run past the receiver rather than stopping in the middle.
Communicate early.
Maintain appropriate spacing in the lines.
The drill should flow continuously without players standing in the kicking lane.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Accuracy of the kick.
Whether players move immediately after disposal.
Communication.
Timing of the run.
Players crossing through the kicking lane.
Quality of marking and gathering.
Flow of the drill.
If lines become long, create additional groups.

commonErrors.error: Player watches the kick and remains stationary
commonErrors.correction: Run immediately after the football leaves the boot.

commonErrors.error: Players collide in the middle
commonErrors.correction: Follow the kick outside the main kicking lane.

commonErrors.error: Receiver is not ready
commonErrors.correction: Demand early voice and eye contact.

commonErrors.error: Kicks become rushed
commonErrors.correction: Require players to balance before kicking.

commonErrors.error: Long waiting lines
commonErrors.correction: Divide players into smaller groups.

progressions: Increase kicking distance.
Require players to use the non-preferred foot.
Add a short lead before receiving.
Introduce two footballs.
Add a handball before the kick.
regressions: Allow players to walk after kicking.
Remove the follow run until kicking accuracy improves.
Use a stationary partner drill first.
matchApplication:
Players must continue working after disposal during a match.
Following the football can create:
A handball receive.
An overlap.
Support at the next contest.
Defensive cover if possession is lost.

title: Moving Target Kicking
primarySkill: Kicking to a Moving Receiver
objective: Teach players to kick accurately to a teammate who is moving rather than standing still. Players learn to place the football into the receiver’s running path so they can mark without slowing down or changing direction.
groundSize:
Medium Area
Approximately 30 m × 20 m
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic Organisation
setup:
Create two lines facing each other approximately 20 metres apart.
Place a starting cone five metres to the side of each receiving line.
The first receiver starts at the side cone rather than directly in front of the kicker.
The football begins with the first player in the opposite line.
howTheDrillWorks:
The receiver begins at the side cone.
The receiver leads diagonally into the space between the two lines.
The kicker waits until the receiver begins moving.
The kicker delivers the football in front of the receiver.
The receiver marks while continuing forward.
The receiver carries the football to the opposite line.
The kicker moves to the receiving line.
The drill repeats in the opposite direction.
The lead should begin before the kick is released.
coachingPoints: Communicate before beginning the lead.
Watch the receiver’s movement.
Kick to where the receiver is going.
Place the football slightly in front of the receiver.
Match the weight of the kick to the speed of the lead.
Avoid kicking directly at the receiver’s current position.
The receiver should accelerate into the football rather than waiting underneath it.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Timing between the lead and kick.
Placement of the football.
Whether receivers slow down.
Communication.
Kicking weight.
Lead direction.
Marking technique while moving.

commonErrors.error: Kick goes behind the receiver
commonErrors.correction: Aim further into the receiver’s running path.

commonErrors.error: Receiver starts too early
commonErrors.correction: Wait until the kicker is balanced and ready.

commonErrors.error: Receiver stops under the football
commonErrors.correction: Kick flatter and further in front.

commonErrors.error: Kicker watches the football instead of the receiver
commonErrors.correction: Scan the receiver before beginning the kicking action.

commonErrors.error: No communication
commonErrors.correction: Require the receiver to call before leading.

progressions: Increase the speed of the lead.
Increase kicking distance.
Add different lead directions.
Use the non-preferred foot.
Add a passive defender following the receiver.
regressions: Allow the receiver to walk through the pattern.
Stop and reset after each repetition.
successIndicators: Allow the receiver to maintain speed.
Time the kick with the lead.
Deliver the football at a markable height.
matchApplication:
Players regularly kick to teammates who are leading into space.
Accurate placement allows the receiver to:
Mark without slowing down.
Play on quickly.
Maintain attacking momentum.
Avoid nearby defenders.

title: Short Approach Drop Punt
primarySkill: Drop Punt from a Short Approach
objective: Progress players from stationary kicking to executing a drop punt after a short, controlled approach. Players learn to coordinate their steps, ball preparation and kicking action without rushing.
groundSize:
Small to Medium Area
Approximately 25 m × 20 m
coachingDifficulty: 1 – Beginner Coach
setup:
Players work in pairs facing each other.
Place a starting cone approximately three metres behind each player’s kicking cone.
Recommended kicking distances:
Under 8–10: 8–10 metres.
Under 12–14: 12–15 metres.
Under 16 and above: 15–20 metres.
Players begin at the rear starting cone.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A begins with the football at the starting cone.
Player A walks or jogs forward for two to four controlled steps.
Player A performs a drop punt from the kicking cone.
Player B marks or gathers the football.
Player B resets at their starting cone.
Player B repeats the short approach and kick.
Continue for the allocated time.
Increase approach speed only when technique remains consistent.
The approach should remain controlled rather than becoming a sprint.
coachingPoints: Prepare the football during the approach.
Keep the final steps controlled.
Maintain balance before contact.
Guide the football onto the boot.
Avoid taking an excessively long final step.
Follow through towards the target.
Continue moving naturally after the kick.
The kicking action should remain similar to the stationary drop punt.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Step rhythm.
Ball preparation.
Balance.
Length of the final stride.
Ball drop.
Accuracy.
Whether the player rushes as speed increases.
Follow-through after disposal.
Reduce the approach speed if technique deteriorates.

commonErrors.error: Player runs too quickly
commonErrors.correction: Slow the approach and regain control.

commonErrors.error: Ball is prepared too late
commonErrors.correction: Position the football before the final two steps.

commonErrors.error: Final stride is too long
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the final step to keep the body balanced.

commonErrors.error: Player stops before kicking
commonErrors.correction: Maintain smooth forward momentum through the kick.

commonErrors.error: Ball drop moves across the body
commonErrors.correction: Guide the football directly over the kicking foot.

progressions: Increase approach speed.
Increase kicking distance.
Add a target gate.
Use the non-preferred foot.
Progress to a continuous running kick.
Receive a handball before beginning the approach.
regressions: Allow players to rehearse the steps without the football.
successIndicators: Coordinate the approach and kicking action.
matchApplication:
Players rarely kick from a completely stationary position during general play.
This drill introduces the movement coordination required to prepare and execute the football while approaching the point of disposal.

title: Ground Ball Gather and Kick
primarySkill: Kicking After a Ground Ball Gather
objective: Develop the ability to collect a ground ball cleanly, accelerate away from the contest and execute an accurate kick. Players learn to secure possession before transitioning quickly into the kicking action.
players: Minimum: 4 Ideal: 8–16 Maximum: 20 using multiple lanes
groundSize:
Medium Area
Approximately 35 m × 20 m
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic Organisation
setup:
Create a straight lane.
Place:
A starting cone.
A ground-ball cone five to eight metres ahead.
A kicking cone another five to eight metres ahead.
A receiving cone 15–25 metres beyond the kicking cone.
A feeder stands beside the ground-ball cone.
Players form lines at the starting and receiving cones.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A runs from the starting cone.
The feeder rolls the football into Player A’s path.
Player A lowers the body and gathers the football cleanly.
Player A accelerates away from the collection point.
Player A prepares the football before reaching the kicking cone.
Player A executes a running drop punt to Player B.
Player B marks or gathers the football.
Player A continues to the receiving line.
Player B returns to the starting line with the football.
Rotate the feeder regularly.
The ground ball should be rolled at a realistic but controllable speed.
coachingPoints: Approach the football with controlled speed.
Lower the hips and keep the head over the ball.
Use two hands whenever possible.
Gather the football cleanly before accelerating.
Take the first steps away from the collection point.
Prepare the football early.
Balance through the running kick.
Players should not attempt to kick before possession is secure.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Approach speed.
Body height.
Hand position.
Clean collection.
Acceleration after the gather.
Ball preparation.
Balance.
Kicking accuracy.
If players repeatedly fumble, reduce the speed of the rolled football.

commonErrors.error: Player bends only at the waist
commonErrors.correction: Lower the hips and bend the knees.

commonErrors.error: Player uses one hand unnecessarily
commonErrors.correction: Gather with two hands whenever space allows.

commonErrors.error: Player looks towards the target before securing the football
commonErrors.correction: Complete the collection before lifting the eyes.

commonErrors.error: Ball preparation is rushed
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate first, then move the football into kicking position.

commonErrors.error: Player kicks while leaning forward excessively
commonErrors.correction: Regain balance during the steps after the gather.

progressions: Increase the speed or angle of the ground ball.
Add a passive defender.
Require the player to change direction after gathering.
Use the non-preferred foot.
Add multiple kicking targets.
Begin with a contested ground ball.
regressions: Allow the player to stop after gathering.
Remove the kicking component until collection improves.
successIndicators: Complete the sequence without unnecessary delay.
matchApplication:
Ground balls regularly begin attacking possessions.
Players must collect cleanly, escape immediate pressure and deliver accurately to a teammate.
This drill applies to:
Loose-ball wins.
Crumbing.
Contested-ball exits.
Defensive rebounds.
Midfield stoppage releases.

title: Contested Gather and Kick
primarySkill: Kicking After Contested Possession
objective: Develop the ability to win or secure a contested ground ball, escape pressure and execute an effective kick. Players learn to place the body between the opponent and the football before creating enough space to dispose accurately.
players: Minimum: 6 Ideal: 10–18 Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
groundSize:
Medium Area
Approximately 35 m × 25 m
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Moderate Management
setup:
Create:
A feeder position.
A contest area approximately six metres wide.
Two exit gates beyond the contest.
One kicking target 20–30 metres ahead.
Two players begin on opposite sides of the contest area.
The feeder stands five to ten metres away with the football.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder rolls or bounces the football into the contest area.
Both players compete to gain possession.
The player who wins the football protects it and exits through either gate.
The opposing player applies controlled pressure without completing a full tackle.
The ball winner accelerates into space.
The ball winner kicks to the target.
Players reset and rotate.
Alternate opponents regularly.
The drill ends if the football becomes trapped for an extended period. Restart with a new feed.
coachingPoints: Approach the football with the body low.
Keep the feet moving.
Position the body between the opponent and the football.
Gather with two hands when possible.
Protect possession.
Exit away from pressure.
Lift the eyes after escaping.
Balance before kicking.
The first objective is to secure possession. The second is to create space for the kick.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Approach to the contest.
Body positioning.
Clean possession.
Ball protection.
Exit decision.
Acceleration away.
Balance.
Quality of the final kick.
Safety of the contact.
Stop the drill if contact becomes uncontrolled.

commonErrors.error: Player reaches without using the body
commonErrors.correction: Win position between the opponent and football first.

commonErrors.error: Player stands upright at the contest
commonErrors.correction: Lower the hips and keep the feet moving.

commonErrors.error: Ball winner tries to kick immediately
commonErrors.correction: Exit pressure before preparing the disposal.

commonErrors.error: Player runs directly into the opponent
commonErrors.correction: Use the open gate away from pressure.

commonErrors.error: Kicking technique collapses under pressure
commonErrors.correction: Regain balance after the exit before kicking.

progressions: Increase opponent pressure.
Add a second kicking target.
Require a handball receive before kicking.
Reduce the size of the exit gates.
Add a recovering defender.
Allow full tackling for appropriately prepared groups.
regressions: Roll the football directly towards one player.
Allow the ball winner to stop after exiting.
successIndicators: Recover quickly after losing the contest.
matchApplication:
This drill replicates possessions that begin with:
A loose ball.
A stoppage spill.
A marking contest.
A defensive ground ball.
A forward-half turnover.
Players must secure possession before creating a usable disposal.
relatedDrills: KK-022 – Ground Ball Gather and Kick

title: Time-Limited Kick
primarySkill: Quick Kicking Execution
objective: Develop the ability to scan, select a target and execute an accurate kick within a limited period. Players learn to prepare before possession and avoid wasting time once the football is secured.
players: Minimum: 6 Ideal: 10–18 Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
groundSize:
Medium Area
Approximately 35 m × 30 m
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic Organisation
setup:
Place one central receiving cone.
Position three targets approximately 20 metres away at different angles.
A feeder stands 10–15 metres from the central receiver.
Players form lines at the feeder, receiver and target positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The receiver scans the target positions.
The feeder passes the football to the receiver.
As the football arrives, the coach begins a countdown.
The receiver must select and kick to a target within the allowed time.
Recommended time limits:
Under 12: Four seconds.
Under 14: Three seconds.
Under 16 and above: Two to three seconds.
The selected target marks or gathers the football.
Players rotate positions.
Continue for the allocated time.
The coach may nominate that one target is unavailable immediately before possession.
coachingPoints: Scan before receiving.
Know the available targets.
Prepare the football immediately.
Take only the steps required.
Remain calm under the countdown.
Select a simple option.
Maintain technical quality.
The time limit should challenge decision speed without making accurate execution impossible.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Scanning before possession.
Time taken to decide.
Ball preparation.
Target selection.
Kicking accuracy.
Whether players panic.
Whether players take unnecessary steps.
